text:
I want to write this out fully, because the short version, 'I had a bad trip and ended up in a psychiatric hospital', doesn't capture what it was like, and because I think the details of how it went wrong could help someone.

Background: I was 24, working in a call centre, living with two flatmates. I'd had depression in my teens, but I'd been okay for a couple of years. I'd taken mushrooms twice and LSD once, all small doses, all positive. My flatmate K had just come back from a festival with some LSD tabs and said they were 'quite strong, maybe split one'. I didn't split it. I took the whole tab on a Saturday afternoon. K took half, and our other flatmate didn't take anything but was home.

The first two hours: the come-up was faster and stronger than anything I'd felt before. Within forty minutes the carpet was rippling and the walls were covered in patterns. That part was fun. We put on music and lay on the floor. K was laughing a lot. I remember feeling very happy and close to her.

The turn: around the two-hour mark, I went to the bathroom. I looked in the mirror and my pupils were enormous, black holes. I stared into them and felt like I was falling in. Behind my eyes there was a corridor, and at the end of the corridor something was waiting. I knew I shouldn't look, but I couldn't stop. When I finally pulled away from the mirror, I felt that something had followed me out. A presence behind my left shoulder. I turned around and nothing was there, but the feeling stayed.

I went back to the living room and tried to tell K. She said 'it's just the acid' and turned the music up. The music had changed. It was something with a heavy bass, and every beat felt like a footstep coming closer. The presence was still behind me. I started glancing over my shoulder every few seconds. K thought it was funny at first, then she stopped laughing.

The fragmentation: the next part is hard to describe in order, because it wasn't in order. I remember the living room lights getting brighter and brighter until everything was white. I remember being in the kitchen with a glass of water and not knowing what water was for. I remember sitting on the floor of my bedroom, holding my knees, rocking. I remember hearing a voice, very clearly, saying my name and then 'it's over now'. I took that to mean my life was over. I remember lying on my bed and feeling my body sinking into it, through it, into the floor, into the building, into the earth, until there was no body and no me, just a heavy, dark pressure and a voice repeating 'it's over now'.

The flatmates: our sober flatmate, J, came into my room at some point. He told me later that I was lying on the bed with my eyes open, not responding, and that when he touched my arm I screamed and backed into the corner. He said I kept saying 'it's over, it's over, I'm already dead'. He tried to talk to me for half an hour. I didn't recognise him. I thought he was the thing from behind the mirror, wearing J's face. K was in her own room, crying, too scared to come in.

The ambulance: J called an ambulance after about an hour of trying to calm me down, because I had started hitting my head against the wall. Two paramedics came, a man and a woman. The woman was very calm and kind. She crouched down and talked to me in a quiet voice. I remember her saying 'you've taken something, it's making you feel this way, it will wear off'. For a moment that made sense, like a door opening. Then the door closed again and I was sure she was lying, that this was how they took you to the place where the dead go.

The hospital: in A&E they gave me a sedative. I remember the needle and a very cold feeling spreading up my arm. I slept, or something like sleep. When I woke up it was night and I was on a trolley in a corridor, and I didn't know how much time had passed. The LSD was still working, but more weakly, and the sedative had made everything heavy and muddy. A doctor came and asked me questions. I couldn't answer most of them. I told her I thought I had died. She wrote something down.

Because I couldn't say clearly that I wasn't going to hurt myself, and because of the head-banging, they admitted me to the psychiatric ward for observation. I was there for four days. The first two days I was still not right. The presence behind my shoulder was still there. Every door slamming made me jump. The other patients scared me, though they were mostly just as frightened as I was. I didn't sleep much. I was ashamed and terrified that I'd broken my mind forever.

On the third day I started to feel more like myself. A psychiatrist talked to me for a long time and said it was very likely a drug-induced episode and that it should pass. On the fourth day they let me go home. My mother came to pick me up. She didn't say a word in the car. I could feel her disappointment and fear like heat.

Afterwards I found out that the tabs K had brought were tested by someone else at the festival and were around 250ug each, maybe more. I had taken a dose far higher than I'd ever had, with no preparation, in a setting that wasn't really safe, after years of depression I'd thought was behind me.

Ich habe zusammen mit meiner Schwester Pilze genommen, an einem Sommertag im Garten unserer Eltern, während sie im Urlaub waren. Meine Schwester hat irgendwann angefangen zu erzählen, dass sie als Kind von unserem Onkel missbraucht wurde. Das wusste ich nicht. Sie hat geweint, und ich war mitten im Trip und konnte nicht klar denken. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass der Garten sich in das Haus unseres Onkels verwandelt und dass ich alles mitansehen muss. Ich habe Bilder gesehen, die ich nicht sehen wollte, und war unfähig, meiner Schwester richtig beizustehen. Ich habe sie nur festgehalten und mit ihr geweint. Gleichzeitig hatte ich das Gefühl, dass ich versagt habe, weil ich als großer Bruder nie etwas gemerkt habe. Der Rest des Nachmittags war ein einziger Albtraum. Wir saßen bis zum Abend unter dem Apfelbaum und haben kaum gesprochen.

LSD at a Halloween party. Everyone in costumes, masks, fake blood. I couldn't tell what was real. A guy in a zombie mask grabbed me as a joke and I completely lost it, screamed, punched him, and ran out into the street. Spent the night hiding behind a church.

Ich habe mit Freunden in einer Wohnung Pilze genommen und dazu einen Horrorfilm geschaut, was im Nachhinein sehr dumm war. Der Film ist sozusagen aus dem Bildschirm herausgekommen. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass die Figuren im Raum sind und dass wir als Nächstes dran sind. Ich bin ins Bad geflüchtet und habe mich eingeschlossen, aber im Spiegel habe ich die Gestalten gesehen, die hinter mir stehen. Meine Freunde haben den Film ausgemacht und versucht, mich zu beruhigen, aber ihre Gesichter sahen aus wie Masken. Ich saß bis zum Morgen auf dem Badezimmerboden.

Mushrooms with my wife on our honeymoon in Costa Rica. Our room was a little cabin in the rainforest. After dark, the jungle noises became overwhelming, howler monkeys, insects, frogs, all screaming at once. I became convinced that something was coming out of the jungle to get us. I spent the night with my back against the door holding a chair leg. My wife was frightened by my fear. It wasn't the honeymoon we planned.

I took ayahuasca in a retreat in Peru. During the ceremony I had visions of my own funeral. I saw my children crying and my wife holding them. I saw my coffin being lowered into the ground and felt the earth falling on me. I was inside the coffin, alive, unable to move or breathe, and I knew no one would ever hear me. The darkness was total, the weight unbearable. I clawed at the inside of the coffin and felt my fingernails break. That went on for what felt like days. When I came back to the maloca, I was lying face down, gripping the mat so hard that my fingers were cramped. The facilitator said it was a 'death and rebirth' and that I should be grateful. I didn't feel reborn. I felt buried.

Ich habe LSD auf einer Hausparty genommen und hatte das Gefühl, mich in die Musik aufzulösen. Am Anfang schön, dann beängstigend, weil ich nicht mehr zurückgefunden habe. Ich wusste stundenlang nicht, ob ich noch einen Körper habe.

My first and only experience with psychedelics was at 19. A friend gave me what he said was 'just a bit of acid'. I didn't know he'd also given me a tab of NBOMe, apparently by mistake. Within an hour my heart was racing, my body felt hot and cold at the same time, and my vision broke into pixels. Then I had a seizure, my friends told me later. I woke up in an ambulance with an oxygen mask on my face, still hallucinating, convinced I was in a spaceship being experimented on. In the hospital I was put on a drip and monitored. I had no idea who these people were or what they were doing to me. I pulled out my IV line and tried to run, and they had to restrain me. It took about twelve hours before I was clear enough to understand where I was. My parents were sitting next to the bed, grey with worry.

Ich habe als Medizinstudentin an einem Wochenende mit Freunden LSD genommen und mich dabei in eine Gedankenspirale über Krankheiten verstrickt. Ich war plötzlich überzeugt, dass ich einen Hirntumor habe, dass ich die Symptome schon lange ignoriert habe und dass ich bald sterben werde. Ich habe alle Symptome, die ich je gelernt habe, an mir gespürt: Kopfschmerzen, Sehstörungen, Taubheit in den Händen. Ich habe meinen Freunden erklärt, dass ich sofort ins Krankenhaus muss, und sie haben mich davon abgehalten, was ich ihnen damals furchtbar übel genommen habe. Ich lag die ganze Nacht wach und habe meinen Körper abgetastet und bin innerlich meine Beerdigung durchgegangen.

I took mushrooms at a forest party and wandered off alone. I found an old abandoned building and went inside. In the dark I heard voices whispering, and I became sure the place was haunted and that the ghosts were trying to keep me there. I couldn't find the exit. I spent what felt like hours wandering through dark rooms, my phone light flickering. When I finally got out, the sun was coming up, and I collapsed on the grass.
High dose of LSD alone. I became convinced I was in hell and that I'd been there forever. My life before was a memory implanted to make the torment worse. I lay on my floor for 8 hours seeing flames.

Ich war mit meinem Freund auf Pilzen in seiner Wohnung, als plötzlich seine Ex-Freundin vor der Tür stand und Sturm geklingelt hat. Sie war betrunken und hat geschrien, dass sie sich etwas antut, wenn er nicht aufmacht. Er hat aufgemacht, und es gab einen furchtbaren Streit mit viel Geschrei und Weinen. Ich saß im Schlafzimmer und habe alles mitgehört, und durch die Pilze war es, als würde der Streit direkt in meinem Kopf stattfinden. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass sie gleich ins Zimmer kommt und mich angreift. Irgendwann hat er die Polizei gerufen, weil sie nicht gehen wollte. Ich habe die ganze Zeit im Schlafzimmer gesessen und mich nicht bewegt.
